title: Resolving regular-unit edge squares
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring and assume the unbounded derived section-module categories exist for every scheme. For a scheme morphism f:X→Y use the fixed section cochain tensor, transported derived tensor, localization Q, exact section pullback F, derived pullback L and its natural isomorphism ε: Q⋙L ≅ F⋙Q, binary maps s=modelTensor over Y and t=modelTensor over X, ordinary oplax tensor arrow β and scalar unit u, and localized regular-unit isomorphisms eY,eX of [def-pd-section-resolving-oplax-constraint-data]. Let μ be a natural tensor arrow L(M⊗N)→LM⊗LN and let v:LQ(1)→Q(1). Assume SectionHypotheses, namely for every flat-term K-flat pair A,B the equation μ(QA,QB)≫(εA⊗εB)≫t(FA,FB) = L(s(A,B))≫ε(A⊗B)≫Q(β(A,B)), and v=ε(1)≫Q(u). Composition here is in Lean order. For every resolving section cochain complex P on Y, SectionUnitEdges Λ f μ v P holds. Explicitly for the left unit the pairModel(1,P), leftVertex1(P), leftVertex2(P), and εP are isomorphisms; μ≫leftVertex1=pairModel≫Qβ, (v▷LQP)≫leftVertex2=leftVertex1≫Q(u▷FP), and regularLeft≫εP=leftVertex2≫Qλ. The opposite branch is L(regularLeft)≫εP=pairModel≫Q(Fλ). The reversed-factor four invertibility assertions and the three right-unit edge squares and opposite branch also hold, with rightVertex1, rightVertex2, right unitor, and the scalar unit in the second factor. These are only edge identities, before composing the whole unit paths.

proof.text: The degree-zero regular unit is resolving directly: tensoring by it is naturally isomorphic to the identity, and its degree-zero term is flat while its other terms are zero and flat. Compare the independent tensorRight with the canonical sheaf-module tensorRight by siteSheafTensorRightIso. Since P is resolving, one-sided invertibility of qTensor makes modelTensor(1,P) and modelTensor(P,1) isomorphisms. Functoriality and the natural-isomorphism components ε make both pairModel maps isomorphisms. The scalar unit sectionTotalUnit is invertible by its identification with the strong monoidal termwise pullback unit.

proof.text: A private general monoidal calculation proves all sixteen unit-edge clauses. The representative equation at (1,P), respectively (P,1), gives the first edge. Substitute v=ε(1)≫Q(u), apply tensor interchange, and use modelTensor naturality for u and the identity to obtain the second edge on each side. The target localization unitor equation and naturality of regularLeft or regularRight in εP give the third edges. The source localization unitor equation, functoriality of L, and naturality of ε at the source unitor give the two opposite branches.

proof.text: The third edges identify each second tensor vertex followed by a mapped unitor with the composite of regularLeft or regularRight and εP. This is invertible, so cancellation of the mapped unitor proves each second vertex invertible. The second edges then prove the first vertices invertible by cancellation of the mapped whiskered scalar unit, using invertibility of v. Assemble these six isomorphism assertions with εP twice, the pair-model isomorphisms, the six edge equalities and the two opposite branches. Thus no preservation-of-K-flatness theorem for the pullback is needed. Whole unit paths remain the parent theorem’s responsibility.
